title: Calibration orchestration + synthetic fuzzing for KV quant profiles: latency vs accuracy study
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Build an orchestration layer and test harness that automates calibration runs for alternative KV cache quantization profiles (per-layer INT8, block-FP8, and hybrid mixes), exercise those profiles under synthetic fuzzed request patterns, and measure accuracy regressions and latency tail behavior.

Context: Prior calibration pipelines focus on static dataset sweeps. We need to understand how calibration frequency and dataset representativeness interact with latency SLOs in production-like workloads (interleaved prompt lengths, multi-turn chat, and KV cache warm/cold ratio). This ticket builds the CI-level orchestration, fuzzed workload generator, and evaluation dashboards for a comprehensive latency vs quality trade-off matrix.

Success criteria:
- Orchestration can run a full calibration + inference sweep end-to-end in <= 8 hours for a single model/config on a 4xA100 farm.
- Produce calibrated profiles (INT8 / FP8 / hybrid) with per-layer scale metadata and a validation report comparing perplexity / token-level BLEU-like metrics vs baseline FP32 and pre-existing INT8 calibration.
- End-to-end report showing 50/95/99.9 Pct latencies and accuracy delta; identify at least one hybrid profile that reduces token-cost by >= 25% with <= 0.6% quality regression on heldout eval.

Planned experiments:
1) Baseline: current production INT8 calibration sweep (existing pipeline).
2) Per-layer dynamic scale: allow per-layer independent integer scale factors and evaluate accuracy drift.
3) Block-FP8: test 8-bit FP variants on KV storage for layers with high activation variance.
4) Hybrid profiles: FP8 for top N layers by variance + INT8 elsewhere.
5) Calibration cadence: offline-only vs daily micro-calib vs streaming incremental calibration.
6) Fuzzed workloads: short-chat heavy, long-context heavy, mixed-ttls, random-prefix repeats to stress KV warm/cold.

Instrumentation: collect per-request latency (p50/p95/p99/p999), CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, quant-scale distributions, and token-level accuracy on holdout. Expose artifacts to the bench dashboard and store raw outputs in s3://redwood-kv-quant/eval/ENG-76321/.

Risk/Notes: calibration may overfit synthetic fuzz distribution; we will keep a strict holdout of production anonymized prompt traces for final validation. Leverage privacy scrubber and legal-approved dataset.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ava Patel: Kickoff meeting with runtime and eval teams. Agreed on metrics, infra targets, and storage layout. Action items: create fuzz generator and orchestration DAG; Marcus to prototype per-layer scale API.

2025-02-14 - Marcus Nguyen: Prototype per-layer scale prototype landed in branch feat/kv-dynamic-scale. Works locally with emulated KV store; observed initial 0.9% drop in token-level accuracy vs FP32 on small sample. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4287
2025-02-16 - Laila Romero (QA): Added fuzzed workload generator. Three modes: chat-short, context-long, and repetition-heavy. S3 artifacts: s3://redwood-kv-quant/fuzzing/ENG-76321/modes.json

2025-02-18 - Marcus Nguyen: First orchestration run (per-layer INT8) on 4xA100 infra. Runtime: 6h34m. Results: p95 latency +4ms compared to baseline; p999 tail increased 11%. Token-level delta: -0.45% vs FP32 on holdout. Dashboard: https://bench.redwood.dev/d/kv-quant/ENG-76321

2025-02-20 - Infra: Observed transient OOM on one node during Block-FP8 runs when KV chunking aligned poorly. Mitigation: added chunk-boundary rounding in runtime and retry with lower batch size. Issue tracked in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/issues/5121

2025-02-21 - PM review (Sofia Klein): Request to prioritize hybrid profiles that trade small accuracy loss for >20% token cost savings. Also asked for a short doc for sales on safe fallbacks for enterprise customers. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/ENG-76321+Report

2025-02-22 - Marcus Nguyen (results): Hybrid experiment (FP8 top-6 layers + INT8 rest) delivered 28% token-cost reduction on bench harness and token-level delta -0.58%. Latency p95 unchanged, p999 improved after chunking fix. Next: run production-sample validation and add drift-simulated daily calib test.
